newsitem.title: USA: DeBakey says Yeltsin normal, cold no problem.
newsitem.headline: DeBakey says Yeltsin normal, cold no problem.

text.p: Noted heart surgeon Michael DeBakey said on Monday President Boris Yeltsin's heart was all but back to normal after surgery two months ago and a cold afflicting the Russian leader should not pose any special problems.

DeBakey, who served as a consultant during Yeltsin's heart bypass surgery in Moscow on Nov. 5, told Reuters Yeltsin's doctors had given him glowing reports about the president's recovery from the operation. "Based on the reports I'm getting, it would appear his cardiac function has been virtually restored to normal," DeBakey said.

He said Yeltsin's recovery was "right on schedule" and the surgery, in which five clogged arteries were bypassed to improve blood flow to the heart, would not leave him susceptible to infections such as a cold.
"It should make him more resistant," DeBakey said.
A government spokesman in Moscow said on Monday the 65-year-old Yeltsin had a "heavy cold" and mild fever and had cancelled several meetings scheduled for the next few days.
DeBakey said the cold was "transient and self-limited" but doctors would keep an eye on it. "Any cold should be taken seriously because it can develop into other things," he said.

Before the surgery, Yeltsin's heart was functioning at greatly reduced levels because of previous heart attacks, which forced him to put aside most of his duties. He went back to work at the Kremlin in late December.

DeBakey said he did not think the president's return to work had contributed to his catching cold. "He promised me he would be a good patient and I think he has been," said DeBakey, who, at 88, continues to perform heart operations at Houston's Methodist Hospital.

Heart bypass patients typically have no subsequent problems with clogged arteries for at least five years following surgery, he said. He said he would likely visit Yeltsin again in the spring when he was to attend a medical meeting in Russia.
